theTwoDefectsCP2CaughtInTHISLANESOWNWORK.defect: THE KEYING TRAP THE FIX ITSELF INTRODUCED, caught by the F1 fixture rather than by review. P-351 made the builder look the declared roll up by the RESOLVED ACCOUNT (`cadLookupKey` is `resolution.accountKey`) instead of by the node's bare prop_id, but the CLI was still handing it `effectiveCadPropertyRoll`, the P-177 REMAPPED view keyed by the SERVED NODE. On a two-keyspace county those are different strings, so the builder's lookup missed every time and the arm retired the county -- the same failure mode as the defect being fixed, arriving through the fix.
theTwoDefectsCP2CaughtInTHISLANESOWNWORK.howItShowedUp: `F1 Hays collision` asserted `recordRetirement` is null and got `{ status: 'retired', ... }`. The assertion was written before the code, which is the whole reason it caught anything.
theTwoDefectsCP2CaughtInTHISLANESOWNWORK.theFix: Two maps over the SAME rows, declared with why: `effectiveCadPropertyRoll` stays keyed by the served node for the CLI's own situs/ring/geometry reads, and a second `builderCadPropertyRoll` keyed by the resolved ACCOUNT is what `buildConformantTier1Payload` is handed. The test builds the builder's view the way the CLI builds it (`accountKeyedBuilderView`), so it cannot prove a keying its caller does not implement.
theTwoDefectsCP2CaughtInTHISLANESOWNWORK.whyItIsRecordedHere: A defect found by a pre-registered falsifier in the same change that fixed the original defect is the single most useful thing this checkpoint can carry: it is evidence the falsifiers are load-bearing, and it is a warning to the integration seat that the two-map shape is not redundant.

theTwoDefectsCP2CaughtInTHISLANESOWNWORK.defect: THE GOLDEN HASH WAS A PLACEHOLDER. F5's byte-identity check (a single-keyspace county must serialise exactly as before) shipped first with the string `PLACEHOLDER` in `PRE_P351_GOLDEN_HASH` -- a test that could not fail, which is the 'a control that cannot fire' shape this program hunts.
theTwoDefectsCP2CaughtInTHISLANESOWNWORK.howItShowedUp: The assertion failed loudly on the placeholder, which is the only reason it was not shipped.
theTwoDefectsCP2CaughtInTHISLANESOWNWORK.theFix: The hash was MEASURED, not asserted: the four changed source files were stashed, a temporary test built the same payload with the same fixture on the pre-change builder, and the SHA-256 of `contentHashForPayload` was recorded (`eba16ad66a51ca86d94e440dd909f00eb095d082da1d46d210f4fc267ea1391b`). The temporary test was then deleted so it cannot be mistaken for the shipped one.
theTwoDefectsCP2CaughtInTHISLANESOWNWORK.residualRiskStated: The golden hash is a hash of a FIXTURE-built payload, not of a real county payload. It proves the builder's serialisation is unchanged for the shapes the fixture carries; it is not a Bastrop byte census. The dispatch asked for 'Bastrop's payloads are byte-identical', and the honest statement of what was proven is the fixture-level one.

theWriterBDecisionRestated.ruled: Writer (b) STAYS IN THE BAKE'S CONTRACT and gets its own instrument.
why: It cannot belong to the gate: it runs INSIDE the bake, after promotion, on the work list the bake built and the run stamp the bake minted, and `requireRetirementGate` runs before the bake exists and cannot see a single excluded node. Moving it is not a refactor, it is a different program.

It must not be dropped either: a node dropped from the work list keeps the PREVIOUS run's publishRunId forever, and the factory's verify-walk requires the CURRENT run id on every row it sweeps, an earned retirement included -- dropping the pass re-opens BP-PUBLISH-RUN-01 on every Hays republish.

So the pass stays, and the guard is the thing it lacked, which is the guard every destructive write in this program lacks (the program trap: 'No writer in this program refuses on blast radius yet (P-320)').
theWriterBDecisionRestated.theInstrument: Before the pass, `accountKeyedBlastRadius(excluded, buildServedKeyspaces(workIds))` measures the excluded set against the served keyspaces this run holds, split by key shape, and `assertAccountKeyedBlastRadius` REFUSES the run when a keyspace has at least one served member and EVERY one of them was excluded. Set equality, not a tuned percentage. `workIds` is read BEFORE the partition, so the measurement is of the population and not of what survived it. The refusal names the keyspace, the excluded count and the served count, and it fires BEFORE `work` is mutated.
theWriterBDecisionRestated.honestLimit: This instrument guards writer (b) ONLY. It would NOT have caught the Williamson emptying, which was writer (a) -- the excluded set there was empty, because every removed node was in the parcel table. Writer (a)'s guard is the resolution itself. Claiming one instrument covers both would be the 'a control that measures one thing does not protect the thing beside it' failure the program trap names.
theWriterBDecisionRestated.blastRadiusToday: Exactly 48209 and 48491 have two served keyspaces.
